story.head: The Jets come in hot
paras: The Jets are on a tear, five straight wins, the last an 8-3 rout of Dallas. The Senators (12-6-2) beat Colorado 4-3 in overtime on Thursday. Going in, the Sens are fourth in the Atlantic (tenth in the NHL) and the Jets sixth in the Central (tied for 16th).
The Senators’ record (.650) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.573), largely because they’re 6-2 in one-goal games. The Jets’ record (.525) is about what their chances are worth.

The Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). They also keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), so good looks are likely to be hard to come by for the Jets. As for the Jets, they ice the puck less than anyone (1st) and create chances on the penalty kill (3rd). They also get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd), and their knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Tim Stützle (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the Senators in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Winnipeg. Drake Batherson (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 20 GP) is next in line. For the Jets, Kyle Connor (16 G / 8 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, with nine points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Ottawa. Mark Scheifele (6 G / 16 A / 22 P in 20 GP) is next in line, with ten points in his last five games.

Samuel Ersson (3-3-2 / .884 SV% in 7 GS) will likely start for Ottawa, and Stuart Skinner (7-4-3 / .886 SV% in 14 GS) for Winnipeg. Skinner has a .931 save percentage in five starts against the Senators, well above his usual .896. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Scott Arniel likes to send Koepke, Barron and Rosén out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Blais, Halliday and Hodgson.

items.text: The Senators are newly without Jonas Johansson, and have been without Warren Foegele and William Eklund for several games. Samuel Ersson is expected to start. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Mammoth are missing more right now.
The Jets are newly without Dylan DeMelo, and have been without Elias Salomonsson and Clay Stevenson for several games. Stuart Skinner is expected to start.
Gabriel Vilardi has two goals on chances worth about 6.1 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Mark Scheifele has a point in five straight games.
